verdict.headline: Oil surges on intercepted Iran strike as chip stocks crater for a fourth straight session
verdict.label: Hold — 4 of 6 indicators breached; oil reverses higher on Iran attack, regime intact — FOMC and Mag-7 earnings Wednesday are the clearing event
verdict.rationale_short: Tuesday ran a tale of two sessions: the Dow gained 1.03% on industrial/consumer earnings and defensive rotation while the Nasdaq fell 0.22% as AMD, Micron, and Marvell extended a four-day chip rout (AMD −8.85% to ~$451; SMH −3%+). The oil picture reversed dramatically late in the session — WTI had opened near $81 on lingering Iran diplomacy optimism, then spiked +4.4% to ~$82.73 after US Central Command announced it intercepted a surprise Iranian attack on US forces in the Middle East; Brent followed to ~$87-88, keeping both oil regime triggers breached. The 10-year yield fell 5bps to 4.60% as pre-FOMC demand absorbed duration; September hike odds remain at ~70%. NVDA recovered to close roughly flat at ~$197 as institutional money narrowed the AI trade to the single irreplaceable GPU name while AMD/Marvell/Intel fell 6–9%. AAPL held near $337 in the second session of quality-rotation buying. Wednesday's FOMC hold (2pm ET; Warsh language on September is the true binary) plus META Q2 and MSFT Q4 FY26 AH (capex ROI trajectory vs AI spend) are the session's clearing events for the full regime.

dont_buy.reason: AMD's −8.85% Tuesday decline continues a four-day structural repricing of the hyperscaler AI capex ROI thesis. Three unresolved inputs — CXMT Chinese memory competition, NVDA circular financing repricing of AI demand reliability, and the MSFT Azure guidance binary Wednesday — all affect AMD's MI400 thesis. Bottom-fishing before Wednesday's FOMC + MSFT earnings binary is position-doubling on the wrong side of the information curve.
dont_buy.better_entry: Post-FOMC AND post-MSFT Azure guidance: if Azure confirms >42% growth with credible AI monetization ROI AND FOMC is explicitly dovish, AMD entry at $440–455 with stop at $430 is defensible. If MSFT capex follows the GOOGL −7% template, AMD faces another leg down toward $410–420.

dont_buy.reason: SMH fell >3% Tuesday for a fourth consecutive session; the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 4.35%. Three simultaneous sector headwinds enter Wednesday: (1) FOMC language on September re-anchors or releases the hawkish trajectory that prices AI capex; (2) MSFT Azure guidance is AMD/NVDA's most important Q3 demand signal; (3) META AI ad ROI vs. $40B+ capex determines commercial justification for infrastructure spend. Adding SMH/SOXX before all three clear is fighting three unresolved binaries without edge.

trade_setups.asset: FOMC rates binary (TBT long / TLT pair)
trade_setups.thesis: Tomorrow's FOMC statement (2pm ET, Warsh press conference 2:30pm) is the year's single highest-information event for rates. Warsh inherits: WTI +4.4% today on Iran military escalation (re-embeds inflation), 30Y at 5.10% (still above 5.00% trigger), September hike probability at ~70%, and a 10Y that fell only 5bps as bond demand is pre-FOMC cautious. The pair captures both outcomes without directional bet: dovish language (September de-emphasized) → TLT long, upgrade clock potentially starts; hawkish language (September explicitly live, tariff CPI embedding acknowledged with oil back above $85) → TBT long, 30Y tests 5.20%, SPX tests 7,380.
trade_setups.entry: Build equal-weight TBT long / TLT long pair into today's close — 16 hours before the decision. Let FOMC July 29 2pm decide which leg converts to directional. Close the losing leg within 30 minutes of the 2pm statement. Hold the winner for 2–3 weeks through August CPI (est. Aug 13).
trade_setups.invalidation: FOMC statement is fully ambiguous — acknowledges both inflation risk and soft growth without explicitly signaling September either way. 10Y holds 4.60% ±2bps post-statement. Flatten both legs within 60 minutes.
trade_setups.horizon: Through FOMC July 29; convert survivor to August CPI hold

bear_case: The four-day consecutive semiconductor selloff is deepening in a way that correlates across geographies — Korean Kospi fell ~10.8% with Samsung and SK Hynix losing 13–15% overnight, which then hit Philadelphia Semiconductor for −4.35% in the US session. This is no longer a single-name story (NVDA circular financing) or a single-country story (China DUV lithography): it is a global repricing of the hyperscaler AI capex ROI narrative at the sector level, and AMD at −8.85% for a second consecutive -8%+ day suggests institutional selling, not just retail panic. The Iran attack interception keeping oil above $85 is a direct headwind to the FOMC's ability to be explicitly dovish tomorrow — Warsh now inherits a Brent ~$87-88 session-close alongside a 30Y still above 5.00% and September hike probability at ~70%, which together make an explicitly dovish statement politically and analytically difficult. If FOMC is a hawkish hold, the 30Y breaks 5.20%, SPX tests 7,380 in the same session that META and MSFT report — and if either company follows GOOGL's −7% capex-without-ROI template, the cascade from 7,428 toward 7,200–7,250 becomes the base case. Bear case invalidation: formal written Iran-US ceasefire (not verbal) before Wednesday open causing oil to reset below $85, AND FOMC explicitly closes September, AND both META/MSFT demonstrate improving AI capex ROI QoQ. All three required simultaneously. If SPX reclaims 7,480 on the post-FOMC Wednesday close, the hold call is wrong.
